evidence.claim: Core Scientific says the project bond market is open and terms unchanged but has no priced AMD bond three months after signing; the 10-Q says financing is needed with no assurance.
evidence.numbers: About $6bn build; $4.4bn commitments; liquidity $1,744mn, -$857mn QoQ; 'capital is the throttle'.

evidence.claim: Riot's Corsicana plan: 80% to 90% non-recourse debt from 2027, with tenant-funded rent credits at an implied 12% if debt is not available on comparable terms.
evidence.numbers: $4.4bn-$4.9bn debt; about $5.5bn capital; about 33% yield on cost; no project debt closed.

evidence.claim: Hut 8 fell 23% on 4 November with Phase 2 financing undated and a smaller free cushion after a $250mn buyback; management now says 'cash will be king'.
evidence.numbers: 1,361 unencumbered BTC; $156.9mn cash; $250mn at about $74.88 vs $48.94 close.

evidence.claim: Cipher's project notes marked down to 100.5, 97.9 and 95.6 of par at 30 September from 104.2, 101.5 and 100.4 at 30 June, despite investment-grade or backstopped rent.
evidence.numbers: Stingray 6.0% notes at 95.6 imply a yield near 7% (our estimate); 41mn new shares in October; $724mn pro forma unrestricted liquidity.

evidence.claim: Jassy said neocloud capacity is 'about 3,500 basis points worse in operating margin' than long-leased capacity, and most AWS capacity is owned or long-leased.
evidence.numbers: Amazon disclosed no third-party MW; leases not yet commenced rose $27.7bn to $164.9bn in 3Q, so leasing grows while the buyer calls neocloud capacity margin-dilutive.

evidence.claim: Selloff after Microsoft capex miss and Alphabet cash burn; Evercore sees hyperscalers burning about $200B over the next year.
evidence.numbers: CoreWeave -11% to $54.34; Nebius -9% to $156.73, though Nebius remains up 87% YTD versus CoreWeave down 24%.

evidence.claim: ASIC told a Senate hearing it is examining the collapse of the A$44B Firmus float, including what banks told buyers about demand. (single source)
evidence.numbers: Filings suggest billions in chip commitments in doubt; US$550M due this year on one site and share handovers if no listing by end-November.

evidence.claim: Hood: 1Q capex incl. finance leases was $45.2bn because some third-party capacity deliveries were delayed; CY26 capex view cut to about $170bn from about $175bn, with spend moving to 2H. Demand still exceeds supply.
evidence.numbers: $45.2bn vs StreetAccount $50.7bn and Microsoft's own 'over $50bn'. After hours CoreWeave fell 5.8%, Nebius 6.3%, IREN 5.3%, Applied Digital 4.3%. Microsoft lost nothing (Azure +48%); the neoclouds carry the delivery slip.

evidence.claim: Galaxy says lenders are 'a lot more conservative' than developers; it will fund Helios Phase III with equity first, seek debt in 1H27, and need not tap credit markets until 1Q-2Q27.
evidence.numbers: Parent put a net $439mn into the Data Centers segment in 3Q26; Phase II notes cost 9.875%; segment notes interest $75.4mn exceeded segment adj. EBITDA $68.7mn.

evidence.claim: Musk predicts stranded compute in half-built data centers and consolidation among more than 200 neoclouds, saying debt markets have almost shut for firms without substantial non-AI revenue.
evidence.numbers: Opinion from an interested party; no data given (single source).

evidence.claim: Shares closed at $54.24, after a 52-week low of $53.50, down about 13% on the week and 54% over a year, market value about $30B; Bernstein downgraded on financing worries.
evidence.numbers: Liabilities $72B against $104B backlog; Benzinga put bond yields above 15.5%.

evidence.claim: JPMorgan Private Bank says lenders now want cash-flow proof. (single source, secondary summary)
evidence.numbers: $266B AI bonds in 2026; CoreWeave CDS record 1,194.5 bps; its 2031 notes touched 16% then near 14%.

evidence.claim: The one neocloud-scale operator with an investment-grade balance sheet: $25B of BBB-tier notes at 5.855% in June, backed by Starlink cash flow rather than GPUs, and a reported $40B Apollo-led package (about $10B loans, $30B IG debt) to buy Nvidia chips, closing in 2027. The CFO expects no further equity after the $85.7B IPO.
evidence.numbers: Q2 AI infrastructure revenue $2.2B against $1.9B of depreciation; capex guided at about $18B a quarter; a 10 GW build is roughly $480B at $60B per GW.
evidence.source: SpaceX Q2 2026 release and call; FT via InvestingLive (6 Oct 2026)

evidence.claim: Meta's non-cancelable commitments, mostly third-party cloud capacity plus servers, network and energy service agreements, jumped again. Hyperscaler take-or-pay contracts are what neocloud lenders rely on.
evidence.numbers: $454.52bn at 30 Sep 2026 vs $349.31bn at 30 Jun and $131.05bn at YE25; due in 2027 $121.41bn (was $81.65bn).

evidence.claim: Meta keeps a contingent obligation to buy up to $14.72bn of cloud capacity over five years. The amount falls if the provider resells the capacity, which is a buyer backstop for a neocloud build. Matching it to Nebius's $15bn resale commitment (Mar 2026) is our inference.
Nebius CRO says price per MW keeps rising in capacity auctions, 2027 capacity would sell out, and Nebius does not carry CoreWeave-style debt.
evidence.numbers: Management talks pricing power while the sector's debt reprices; no dollar figures given (CNBC via Slicast).

evidence.claim: Unsecured notes trade near 80 cents (about 15% yield) and five-year CDS hit about 1,128–1,195 bps, implying roughly 45–60% odds of default within five years.
Microsoft ended its anchor lease at Nscale's 90 MW Loughton site after the grid date slipped to the early-to-mid 2030s, weeks before Nscale's NYSE IPO at up to $35B.
evidence.numbers: Microsoft and Anthropic are about 85% of Nscale's backlog; Nscale says other contracts are unaffected.

evidence.claim: Firmus pulled a near-$5B IPO and AirTrunk delayed its REIT listing to 2027.
Banks would not underwrite Volta's $3.7B GPU term loan, selling it best-efforts at about 11.2% to 11.75%.
evidence.numbers: Only the $1.3B lease-backed piece was guaranteed (single source).

evidence.claim: Closed a $1B loan at 6.78% fixed, rated Baa1, against contracts with two investment-grade customers, and is raising up to $4B of equity.
SemiAnalysis says neocloud power contracting stalled from Q3 2025 as credit tightened.

question: Can neoclouds keep raising money below what their assets earn?
summary: October repriced weak-credit compute and the last week did not reverse it: CoreWeave fell 11% to $54.34 on 30 October with CDS touching a record 1,194.5 bps, Firmus's failed A$44B float now faces an ASIC review with chip payments due, and Nscale still has no price range against a $30-35B target as investors push $16-19B. Microsoft's capex miss and Alphabet's -$9.1B free cash flow raise doubt about the buyers themselves. Nebius says prices per MW are still rising, so the gap is between strong pricing talk and costly money. Secured loans against strong customers remain open. 5 November: landlord peers still have unpriced project debt (Core Scientific AMD, Hut 8 Phase 2, Riot Corsicana), with Riot offering a 12% tenant fallback.
title: Neocloud funding access
